what_its_for: Sodium fluoride rinse helps protect your teeth from cavities (tooth decay). It strengthens the outer layer of your teeth (enamel) and helps prevent new cavities from forming. It is often recommended for people who are at high risk for cavities, those wearing braces, or people with dry mouth.
how_to_take: Rinse your mouth with this solution once daily, usually at bedtime after brushing your teeth. Measure the correct amount (usually 10 mL or 2 teaspoons) and swish it around your mouth for 1 full minute. Then spit it out completely — do NOT swallow it. Do not eat, drink, or rinse your mouth with water for at least 30 minutes after using this rinse. This allows the fluoride to fully coat and protect your teeth.
dosing: Adults and children 6 years and older: Use 10 mL (about 2 teaspoons) once daily. Children under 6 years old: Do NOT use unless your dentist or doctor specifically tells you to. Always follow the exact dose your dentist or doctor recommends. Do not use more than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still before bedtime. If it is the next morning, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular routine. Do NOT use two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep this product out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze. Check the expiration date on the bottle and throw it away if it is expired.
what_to_avoid: Do not swallow this rinse — if you or your child accidentally swallows a large amount, call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) right away. Do not eat, drink, or rinse your mouth with water for at least 30 minutes after using this product. Avoid giving this product to children under 6 years of age unless directed by a dentist or doctor. Do not use more than the recommended dose, as too much fluoride can cause white spots or streaks on teeth (dental fluorosis).
when_to_call_doctor: Call your dentist or doctor if you notice white, brown, or black spots or streaking on your teeth (this may be a sign of too much fluoride). Also call if you or your child accidentally swallows more than a small amount of this rinse, if you develop mouth irritation, rash, or allergic reactions (such as swelling, hives, or difficulty breathing), or if your teeth seem to be getting worse or not improving over time.
when_it_works: Sodium fluoride rinse works gradually over time. You will not feel it working right away. Consistent daily use over several weeks to months helps build up protection in your teeth and reduces the risk of new cavities. Keep using it as directed even if you do not notice immediate results.
special_populations: Children: This rinse is generally safe for children 6 years and older when used as directed. Children under 6 should NOT use this product due to the risk of swallowing it. Always supervise children while they use this rinse. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: This rinse is considered safe to use during pregnancy and breastfeeding when used as directed and not swallowed. Talk to your doctor or dentist if you have concerns. Kidney Disease: People with severe kidney problems should check with their doctor before using fluoride products regularly. Elderly: This product is generally safe for older adults. It may be especially helpful for seniors who have dry mouth or are at higher risk for cavities.
